title: The cobra’s shade
told: a sakhi from the Janamsakhis, a traditional story

hook.say: before the story, a question. have you ever been protected by something you didn’t arrange?
options: then you know this feeling. listen.
then you’ll love this one. listen.
maybe you just didn’t see it. listen.

steps.line: A hot afternoon beyond Talwandi. Young Nanak had been sent to watch the family’s buffaloes. His father hoped it would teach him responsibility.
steps.label: a traditional sakhi

steps.line: But the boy lay down under a tree and fell asleep in the heat. Slowly the sun moved, and the shade slid off his face.

steps.q: The sun is on his face. A cobra slides out of the grass. What do you think it does?
o: Coils in his shadow to keep cool
Spreads its hood over his face
Lies across his chest, keeping guard
steps.why: It spread its hood over his face like an umbrella. The most dangerous thing in the field became his shelter.

steps.line: A cobra slid up beside him, raised itself, and spread its hood wide over his face, like a small umbrella.
Rai Bular, the village landlord, came riding by and saw it. He didn’t reach for a stick. He understood that this boy was under God’s protection.

steps.q: Indian listeners had heard of a serpent’s hood sheltering someone before. Whom?
o: Rama, on his way into exile
steps.why: After his awakening, the serpent king Mucalinda coiled around the Buddha and spread his hood over him through a storm. Vishnu, too, rests beneath Shesha’s hoods. Listeners knew the picture: this one is special.

steps.line: From that day, Rai Bular honored the boy, and defended him to his worried father more than once.

steps.q: His father worried about him often. Once he gave Nanak money to make a good deal at market. What did Nanak do?
o: Bought goods to sell, as he was told
Fed a group of hungry holy men
Gave it to Rai Bular to keep safe
steps.why: He called it sacha sauda, the true bargain. His father was furious; Gurdwara Sacha Sauda stands on the spot today.

steps.q: Another day, Nanak’s buffaloes strayed into a neighbor’s field while he sat lost in thought. The farmer brought Rai Bular to see. What did they find?
o: The buffaloes still grazing in it
steps.why: The field was whole. Gurdwara Kiara Sahib marks it today in Nankana Sahib, Pakistan, the old Talwandi, and Rai Bular grew surer still.

say: is it history? the sources can’t say, and it’s honest to admit that. many sikhs treasure it as a true event. many others hear it as a sakhi: a story told to show something true.
and what it shows is lovely. sikhs speak of god as the protector who keeps those who remember. the story puts it in one picture: a hood spread wide over a sleeping face.

steps.q: From the story, why does it matter that Rai Bular, not the family, saw it?
o: He owned the land, so his word settled it
A Muslim neighbor saw what his family didn’t
He was the boy’s teacher at the time
steps.why: Sikhs remember Rai Bular, with Nanak’s sister Nanaki, as among the first to see who Nanak was. It came from outside the family, and across faiths.

today.say: today, if you can, sit in some shade for two minutes: a tree, a porch, the cool side of a room. bring to mind one time you were sheltered without arranging it, and say thank you, to god or to life. your choice.
options: then let the thanks land. you were kept.
that’s okay. the shade itself is today’s shelter.

card.keepWhy: Even the fierce thing can shelter you.
